01-Concepts/macro/Central Bank Buying.md: Sovereign gold accumulation above 1,000 tonnes per year since 2022; a price insensitive demand floor that broke the real rates gold link
01-Concepts/macro/Central Bank Intervent: A central bank buying or selling its own currency to steer the rate; produces gap moves that stops and risk models cannot survive
01-Concepts/macro/Central Bank Policy.md: Rate and balance sheet tools that set the cost of money; hits commodities through the USD, demand, and financing channels
01-Concepts/macro/Chokepoint.md: Narrow maritime straits carrying most seaborne oil; the largest source of geopolitical risk premium, worst when spare capacity is thin
01-Concepts/macro/Commodity Currencies.m: Exchange rates of resource exporters that track their dominant export; a liquid FX proxy for expressing commodity views
01-Concepts/macro/DXY Correlation.md: Persistent inverse link between the trade weighted dollar and USD priced commodities; a regime filter that supply shocks can override
01-Concepts/macro/Geopolitical Risk.md: The risk premium markets pay for potential supply disruptions; small and persistent but asymmetric, best traded through out of the money options
01-Concepts/macro/Green Metals.md: Copper, nickel, lithium, cobalt, and rare earths critical to electrification; policy driven structural demand running against slow mine supply
01-Concepts/macro/Intervention.md: Central bank entering FX to move its own currency; the primary tail risk in carry trades, gapping violently through stops
01-Concepts/macro/Macro Regime.md: Growth and inflation combined into 4 quadrants; the highest level strategic call that determines which asset classes and factors work
01-Concepts/macro/Monetary Policy Diverg: Central banks moving rates in opposite directions; the strongest persistent FX trend driver, reversing violently when the rate gap narrows
01-Concepts/macro/Petrocurrency.md: Currency of an oil exporter linked to crude through the trade balance; NOK, CAD, RUB, BRL, MXN as tradeable oil proxies
01-Concepts/macro/Real Interest Rates.md: Nominal rates minus inflation, quoted directly by TIPS yields; the dominant driver of gold and the opportunity cost for all assets
01-Concepts/macro/Real Rates Regime.md: The prevailing level and direction of inflation adjusted rates; a single dial carrying -0.7 to -0.9 correlation with gold
01-Concepts/macro/Regime Shift.md: A fundamental change in the data generating process; correlations and vol reset, breaking strategies calibrated on the prior regime
01-Concepts/macro/Risk-On Risk-Off.md: Markets oscillating between chasing risk and fleeing to safety; cross asset correlations spike as everything moves as one risk factor
01-Concepts/macro/Safe Haven Assets.md: Instruments that hold value in crises through negative tail correlation; gold, Treasuries, JPY, CHF, USD, with initial liquidation risk
01-Concepts/macro/Spare Capacity.md: Idle oil production that can restart within 90 days; the buffer that caps prices and sizes the geopolitical risk premium
01-Concepts/macro/Supply Shock.md: Sudden change in commodity availability forcing rapid repricing; the temporary versus permanent duration call decides whether to fade or trend
01-Concepts/macro/TIPS Breakeven.md: Nominal yield minus TIPS yield, the market's expected inflation; separates real rate moves from nominal, the distinction that drives gold
01-Concepts/macro/Terms of Trade Shock.m: A sudden large swing in a country's export to import price ratio from commodity moves; the currency adjusts over 3 to 12 months, creating persistent tradeable FX trends
01-Concepts/macro/Terms of Trade.md: The ratio of a country's export prices to import prices; the strongest fundamental predictor of commodity linked currencies, with backtest Sharpe near 0.5
01-Concepts/macro/Yield Curve Slope.md: The 10Y minus 2Y spread (2s10s), the market's cleanest cycle gauge; inversion leads recessions and four steepening or flattening regimes read the growth and policy path
01-Concepts/market-structure/0DTE.md: Options that expire the same trading day, now near 50% of SPX volume, where dealer gamma hedging drives intraday moves that leak into FX and commodities
01-Concepts/market-structure/Arbitrageur: Trader who buys the cheap leg and sells the dear leg of a mispricing, enforcing the law of one price across futures curves and FX cross rates
01-Concepts/market-structure/Arrival Pri: The mid price at the instant an order is submitted, the primary benchmark for execution quality measured as implementation shortfall against the fill
01-Concepts/market-structure/Ask.md: The higher side of a two way quote, the price you pay to buy immediately; ask depth shows how much size you can lift before price runs away
The obligation forced on a short option holder when the buyer exercises, turning collected premium into a live position with margin calls and pin risk
01-Concepts/market-structure/Backwardati: LME physical tightness that drives cash above the 3 month forward, forcing shorts who cannot source metal into unbounded loss buybacks, as in the 2022 nickel spike
01-Concepts/market-structure/Basis Point: 0.01%, the standard unit for quoting rate moves, swap spreads, and yield differentials; misreading it as a full percent is a 100x error
01-Concepts/market-structure/Bid.md: The lower side of a two way quote, the price you receive when selling immediately; bids vanish fast on bad news, worsening fills for sellers who wait
The round number handle of an FX rate that dealers omit when quoting, and a psychological level where option barriers and stop clusters concentrate
01-Concepts/market-structure/Cable.md: Desk slang for GBP/USD, named after the 1866 transatlantic telegraph cable, driven by Bank of England policy and UK political risk
01-Concepts/market-structure/Cancel.md: Withdrawing a resting order before it fills, where the round trip latency window leaves it exposed to being picked off on a stale quote
01-Concepts/market-structure/Cancelled W: LME warrants flagged for withdrawal, a leading indicator of physical metal demand; a high cancellation ratio signals shrinking deliverable supply and squeeze risk
01-Concepts/market-structure/Cash Settle: Settling a derivatives position by exchanging the cash difference against a reference index instead of physical delivery, which opens markets to financial traders but adds basis risk
01-Concepts/market-structure/Cathode.md: The 99.99% pure refined copper deliverable on the LME, where regional premiums above the benchmark reveal where metal is tight and arb flows redirect supply
01-Concepts/market-structure/Central Lim: The centralized book matching all buy and sell orders by price time priority, the foundation of exchange price discovery; FX has no consolidated equivalent
01-Concepts/market-structure/Charter Par: The written contract that hires a ship, where clause wording on laytime, demurrage, and off hire can move more money than the headline freight rate
01-Concepts/market-structure/Concentrate: The intermediate ore product that must be smelted into refined metal, whose tightness leads refined copper prices by 3 to 6 months through TC/RC signals
01-Concepts/market-structure/Cross Pairs: Currency pairs with no USD leg, isolating the bilateral relationship between two economies; useful for relative exporter views like AUD/CAD or NOK/SEK
01-Concepts/market-structure/Currency Pa: The fundamental FX unit quoting a base currency in units of a quote currency; every trade simultaneously buys the base and sells the quote
01-Concepts/market-structure/Dark Pool.m: A private venue where orders stay hidden until they match, cutting market impact and front running on large flows at the cost of uncertain, often partial fills
01-Concepts/market-structure/Delivery.md: The physical settlement of expiring futures that forces convergence to spot via arbitrage; the April 2020 negative WTI print came from delivery gridlock at Cushing
01-Concepts/market-structure/Dry Bulk ve: Splits freight into solid cargo on bulk carriers versus liquid cargo on tankers; mechanically separate fleets with their own indices, demand drivers, and no cross hedging
01-Concepts/market-structure/ECN.md: Anonymous central limit order book matching interbank FX without a dealer; EBS and Reuters Matching set the benchmark spot price feeding every other venue
01-Concepts/market-structure/EM Currenci: Developing economy currencies paying 5 to 15 points of carry above USD to compensate for devaluation, intervention, and capital control risk; often traded via NDFs
01-Concepts/market-structure/Exercise.md: The buyer's act of invoking an option to transact at the strike; American versus European style sets when, and residual time value governs whether to exercise early or sell
The day a derivative dies, forcing delivery, cash settlement, or a roll; roll cost or gain is set by contango versus backwardation on the curve
01-Concepts/market-structure/Expiry Pinn: Spot gravitates toward a large option strike near expiry as dealers hedging long gamma buy dips and sell rallies; the magnet vanishes once options roll off
01-Concepts/market-structure/FOK.md: Fill or Kill order demanding the full size execute at once or cancel entirely; used for spread legs and hedges where a partial fill creates naked risk
01-Concepts/market-structure/FX Market H: The 24/5 rotation through Sydney, Tokyo, London, and New York sessions; liquidity peaks in the London New York overlap, driving spreads and slippage by hour
01-Concepts/market-structure/FX Swap.md: Simultaneous spot exchange plus a reversing forward, packaged as one trade; the largest FX instrument by turnover, used for funding not direction and priced in swap points
01-Concepts/market-structure/Fiber.md: Desk slang for EUR/USD, the most traded pair at roughly 23% of turnover; its moves drive the dollar index and every dollar priced commodity
01-Concepts/market-structure/Fill.md: The execution of an order defined by price, quantity, and timestamp; partial fills and slippage make fill quality a core measure of execution performance
01-Concepts/market-structure/Flat.md: Holding no position, an active choice to carry no risk, often taken before binary events like NFP or OPEC and at desk handover
01-Concepts/market-structure/Force Majeu: Contract clause voiding a delivery obligation when extraordinary events make performance impossible; it removes contracted supply instantly, tightening prompt spreads while the flat price barely moves
01-Concepts/market-structure/Forward Con: Private OTC agreement to trade an asset at a set price on a future date, fully customizable but carrying bilateral credit risk and settling at maturity
01-Concepts/market-structure/Forward Fre: Cash settled swap on a Baltic freight route, letting a trader fix a shipping rate on paper months ahead with no vessel involved
01-Concepts/market-structure/Freight Opt: Asian style options on FFA routes settling against the average Baltic assessment; pay a premium to cap or floor freight cost while keeping favourable moves
01-Concepts/market-structure/Front Month: The nearest expiring active futures contract, most liquid and tightest, where physical tightness shows first; the M1 minus M2 spread reads near term supply and demand
01-Concepts/market-structure/Futures Con: Standardized exchange traded agreement cleared through a clearinghouse with daily mark to market and posted margin; the backbone of commodity price discovery and hedging
01-Concepts/market-structure/G10 Currenc: The 10 most liquid developed market currencies forming 45 pairs and 80% of FX turnover; the default universe for systematic carry, momentum, and value strategies
01-Concepts/market-structure/Grains.md: CBOT agricultural futures in corn, wheat, soybeans, and rice; seasonal and WASDE driven, where weather shocks in key regions can trigger 30 to 50% rallies
01-Concepts/market-structure/Hard Commod: Mined or extracted resources like energy and metals with long supply lead times and indefinite storage; delayed supply response drives multi year boom and bust cycles
01-Concepts/market-structure/IOC.md: Immediate or Cancel order that fills whatever liquidity is available now and discards the rest, never resting on the book; the default aggressor type for taking depth without revealing total size
01-Concepts/market-structure/Internaliza: Dealers crossing opposing client orders on their own book instead of hedging externally, capturing the full spread risk free; top FX banks internalize 60 to 80% of spot, shrinking public price discovery
01-Concepts/market-structure/LME Prompt: The LME structure where every business day out to 3 months is a separate tradeable date rather than a monthly expiry, enabling granular Cash to 3M and Tom/Next spread trades on physical tightness
01-Concepts/market-structure/Last Look.m: The dealer's right to reject a client trade within a 50 to 200 ms window after submission; a free option on client flow and one of the largest hidden costs in FX execution
01-Concepts/market-structure/Laytime, De: The voyage charter time framework where exceeding the loading and discharge allowance triggers daily demurrage penalties while beating it earns half rate despatch; the largest source of cash leakage on a fixture
01-Concepts/market-structure/Limit Order: An order setting the worst acceptable price that guarantees price but not fill, resting in the book until executed; trades slippage for opportunity cost and provides the liquidity market makers earn spread on
01-Concepts/market-structure/Lit Venue.m: A trading venue where all resting orders are publicly visible in the order book, giving full price transparency but leaking intent on large orders; CME, ICE, LME, and FX ECNs are lit
01-Concepts/market-structure/Long.md: Owning an asset to profit from a price rise; in FX every long is automatically short the quote currency, and crowded longs cascade via stop losses
01-Concepts/market-structure/Major Pairs: The 7 USD versus G10 pairs (EUR/USD, USD/JPY, GBP/USD and others) that dominate FX turnover with the tightest spreads and deepest books; the starting universe for systematic FX and USD macro views
01-Concepts/market-structure/Mark to Mar: Revaluing a position at the current price rather than entry, settled daily on futures with cash credited or debited from margin; the mechanism that stops credit risk accumulating and triggers margin calls
01-Concepts/market-structure/Market Orde: An order executing immediately at the best available price, guaranteeing fill but not price and sweeping deeper levels on size; the tool when speed of exit matters more than slippage cost
01-Concepts/market-structure/Matching En: The exchange software pairing orders by price time or pro rata priority in microseconds; its queue rules and fairness mechanisms (speed bumps, batch auctions) directly determine fill quality and strategy edge
01-Concepts/market-structure/Multi Deale: An electronic venue (FXGO, 360T, FXall) where multiple banks stream competing bilateral quotes the client compares and picks; competitive tension tightens spreads but pricing is client specific by flow toxicity
01-Concepts/market-structure/NDF.md: A cash settled FX forward paying the rate difference in USD instead of delivering a restricted EM currency; the primary hedge and carry access for CNY, KRW, INR, and BRL under capital controls
01-Concepts/market-structure/Notional.md: The face value of a trade on which PnL, margin, and risk are calculated, not cash exchanged; it scales every risk metric and is the root of most fat finger sizing errors
01-Concepts/market-structure/Open Intere: The stock of futures or option contracts still open, distinct from volume; read with price direction it reveals whether a move carries new conviction or is just short covering and position unwinding
01-Concepts/market-structure/Option.md: A contract granting the right but not obligation to buy (call) or sell (put) at a strike, with capped premium loss and asymmetric payoff; the instrument for hedging one direction and trading volatility
01-Concepts/market-structure/Partial Fil: When only part of an order executes and the remainder works on, leaving a half hedge plus a chase, wait, or cancel decision; routine even in EUR/USD and the norm in thin far dated contracts
01-Concepts/market-structure/Physical vs: The two ways to take a freight view: chartering real steel with operational alpha and capital tied up, versus cash settled FFAs on a Baltic index; the core desk capital allocation question, with basis as residual
01-Concepts/market-structure/Pip.md: The smallest standard FX price increment, 0.0001 for most pairs and 0.01 for JPY, the universal unit for spreads, stops, and PnL whose dollar value varies by pair and position size
01-Concepts/market-structure/Platts Wind: The 30 minute daily Market on Close where physical houses submit public bids and offers that set Dated Brent and other benchmarks underpinning trillions in contracts; a real time read on physical tightness
01-Concepts/market-structure/PnL.md: Profit and loss, realized plus unrealized; the daily scorecard driving risk limits, capital allocation, and trader compensation.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Port Conges: Vessels queuing at anchor shrink effective fleet supply without changing fleet size; anchorage counts lead the Baltic dry indices.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Position.md: Your current holding by instrument, direction, and size; the state that generates PnL as prices move.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Realized Pn: Locked in profit or loss from closed trades; the permanent, bonus and tax relevant measure of performance.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Refinery Ut: Throughput as a percent of operable capacity; links crude demand to product supply and drives crack and calendar spread moves.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Shadow Flee: Aging, opaque, uninsured tankers moving sanctioned oil; enforcement intensity sets the discount on capped grades and mainstream freight demand.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Short.md: Owing an asset to profit from a price fall; unlimited downside makes shorts more prone to blowups than longs.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Single Deal: A bank's proprietary FX venue streaming tailored prices with last look; handles 60 to 70 percent of spot volume with hidden execution costs.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Soft Commod: Grown tropical crops with biological supply lag; weather and disease shocks trend for years and resist mean reversion.
Non commercial trader taking price risk for profit with no physical exposure; supplies the liquidity that lets hedgers offload risk.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Spot Rate.m: Current price for immediate (T+2) currency exchange; the anchor from which forwards, swaps, and options are priced.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Stop Loss.m: Order that converts to a market order at a set level to cap trade losses; gaps can breach the intended limit.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Swap.md: OTC fixed for floating cash exchange over a commodity index; a strip of forwards and the primary custom hedging tool for producers.
01-Concepts/market-structure/TC In and T: Operator rents a ship in at fixed cost then relets or trades it out; the sublet spread is a directional freight position.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Tank Tops.m: Crude storage near full capacity forcing shut ins and deep discounts; the condition behind April 2020's negative WTI print.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Tick.md: Smallest price increment an instrument can move; sets the minimum spread and, times contract size, the dollar PnL per tick.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Time Charte: Hiring a whole ship at a fixed daily rate while paying voyage costs; the period rate embeds the freight forward curve.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Trading Tax: A trading seat is a point on 8 orthogonal axes such as capital, decision, and liquidity, not a single label like prop versus discretionary.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Turnaround: Scheduled spring and fall refinery maintenance that cuts crude runs; predictable in timing, variable in magnitude, traded via calendar spreads.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Unrealized: Mark to market profit on open positions; changes every tick, consumes margin, and triggers calls when a position goes offside.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Vessel Clas: Standard dry bulk size bands from Handysize to VLOC plus payload capacity; matching hull to route and berth decides voyage economics.
01-Concepts/market-structure/Volume.md: Count of contracts traded in a session; a flow measure that confirms conviction behind a price move, unlike open interest which counts live positions
01-Concepts/market-structure/Voyage Char: The 2 ways to hire a ship, splitting who pays bunkers and bears freight risk; the first risk decision that tells a freight trader what to hedge
The spot freight contract paying an owner a fixed rate per tonne while the owner burns bunkers and absorbs delay, locking the trader's transport cost
01-Concepts/market-structure/Warrant.md: LME document of title to a warehouse metal lot; cancellations signal physical buyers pulling metal and anchor futures prices to the physical market
01-Concepts/market-structure/Wet Tanker: The tanker size ladder from MR to VLCC crossed with the dirty versus clean split, fixing which cargoes a ship lifts and which freight market prices it
01-Concepts/microstructure/Adverse Selec: The market maker's risk that a quote is a free option to better informed counterparties; the single largest cost in FX making, managed through tiering, last look, and markout
01-Concepts/microstructure/Aggregated Da: Tick events compressed into OHLCV bars for medium frequency research, trading path detail for tractability; bar size and boundary alignment materially shift backtest results
01-Concepts/microstructure/Bid-Ask Sprea: The gap between best bid and ask that prices immediacy; every round trip costs at least one spread, dominating cost for high turnover spread traders
01-Concepts/microstructure/Client Tierin: Charging each client a spread scaled to their historical markout toxicity; the primary OTC defense that lets dealers keep profitable uninformed flow while pricing informed flow out
01-Concepts/microstructure/Depth of Book: Resting order volume at every price level beyond top of book; the primary input for estimating large order market impact and a warning signal when depth evaporates before news
Predictive signals from the direction and urgency of customer order flow; banks seeing 10 to 15% of global FX detect macro shifts days before price, outsiders reconstruct weaker versions from ECN tapes
01-Concepts/microstructure/Half Spread.m: Half the bid ask spread, the cost of a single trade from mid; the fundamental unit of FX transaction cost analysis and a maker's gross revenue per side before adverse selection
01-Concepts/microstructure/Inventory.md: The net position a market maker accumulates as a byproduct of quoting, not by choice; flattening it quickly while earning the spread is the central making challenge
01-Concepts/microstructure/Liquidity.md: The ease of trading size without moving price, measured by spread, depth, volume, and Kyle's lambda; concentrated in front months and evaporates precisely when you need to exit
01-Concepts/microstructure/Market Impact: The price movement your own trade causes, split into reversing temporary and lasting permanent components; scales as the square root of size over ADV and caps tradeable position size
01-Concepts/microstructure/Markout.md: Post trade price movement measured over a fixed horizon; the primary tool for scoring execution quality, flow toxicity, and market making profitability
01-Concepts/microstructure/Mid Price.md: Arithmetic average of best bid and ask; the TCA benchmark for execution quality, but misleading when the book is thin or skewed
01-Concepts/microstructure/Positioning S: Contrarian read of aggregate net long or short data from COT and surveys; extreme positioning flags crowded trades vulnerable to violent unwinds
01-Concepts/microstructure/Quote.md: A price shown to the market signaling willingness to buy or sell at that level; the fundamental act of market making
01-Concepts/microstructure/Quoting.md: Continuously streaming bid and ask prices as the core market maker activity; an engine skews quotes for inventory, volatility, and adverse selection
01-Concepts/microstructure/Round Trip.md: A buy plus a sell of the same instrument; you pay half a spread per leg, setting the minimum cost any strategy must beat
01-Concepts/microstructure/Skew Microstr: Asymmetry between bid side and ask side order book volume; one of the most reliable directional predictors at horizons under 10 seconds
01-Concepts/microstructure/Slippage.md: The gap between intended and actual fill price from spread crossing, impact, and delay; the difference between a backtest and reality
01-Concepts/microstructure/Sniping.md: Hitting a maker's stale quote before it refreshes for near risk free profit; the edge is latency, not fundamental value
01-Concepts/microstructure/Stale Quote.m: A price not refreshed after the market moved; a guaranteed loser for the quoter and the primary source of sniping losses
01-Concepts/microstructure/Sweep.md: A large aggressive order consuming multiple book levels at worsening prices; the primary market impact mechanism and a signal of informed urgency
01-Concepts/microstructure/Tick Data.md: Every trade and quote update recorded with microsecond timestamps; the raw material for microstructure research, demanding heavy storage and noise handling
01-Concepts/microstructure/Top of Book.m: The best bid and ask forming the BBO, the tightest immediate execution price; silent on available size beyond the first units
01-Concepts/microstructure/Toxic Flow.md: Client flow that consistently predicts price moving against the maker who filled it; the empirical face of adverse selection measured through markouts
01-Concepts/microstructure/Turnover.md: How frequently positions are flattened and reestablished; it multiplies round trip cost and sets the per trade alpha hurdle a strategy must clear
01-Concepts/microstructure/Two Way Price: A simultaneous bid and ask shown together, forcing the counterparty to declare direction; the standard convention of market making
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/API Gr: Inverted density scale for crude where higher means lighter oil; drives refined product yield, refinery fit, and grade price differentials
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/ATM.md: Option strike set at the forward rate, carrying maximum time value and zero intrinsic; the headline vol that anchors the entire FX surface
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Backwa: Profit from rolling a long future when the front sits above the deferred; a persistent commodity carry return that mirrors FX carry
Downward sloping curve where deferred delivery trades below nearby, signaling tight near term supply and paying long positions positive roll yield
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Ballas: Pricing the empty repositioning voyage into the freight quote so round trip TCE, not the laden rate, reflects true vessel earnings; often halves the daily figure
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Barrie: Exotic whose payoff switches on or off when spot touches a level (knock in or knock out); cheaper than a vanilla and the dominant FX exotic flow
Difference between 2 reference prices, usually spot minus futures or across locations and grades; the raw material of every relative value trade
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Bunker: Marine fuel grades split by sulphur and refining, 40 to 60 percent of voyage cash cost; hedged with gasoil futures or port index swaps that carry basis risk
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Butter: Average 25 delta wing vol minus ATM vol, measuring smile curvature; a volga trade that prices tail risk and widens ahead of binary events
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/CFD Cr: Weekly spread between Dated Brent and front month Brent futures; the most sensitive real time read on physical crude tightness, not a retail FX CFD
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Call O: Right to buy at a fixed strike for a premium; the buyer risks only the premium for convex upside while a naked writer faces unbounded loss
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Carry: Systematic factor harvesting the yield of high over low assets across FX, rates, commodities, and equities; positive on average but exposed to correlated crash unwinds
Borrow a low rate currency to fund a higher rate one and pocket the differential; profitable on average, subject to violent unwinds when risk aversion spikes
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Cash t: LME cash minus 3 month forward, the single most important gauge of base metal physical tightness and a leading indicator for flat price direction
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Contan: Rent, insurance, and financing cost that caps LME contango width; when contango exceeds carry, a cash and carry arb pulls the spread back
Loss from rolling a long future when deferred sits above nearby; the hidden drag that makes commodity ETFs bleed even as spot rises
Upward sloping forward curve where deferred futures trade above nearer ones; passive longs bleed negative roll yield rolling up the curve
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Conven: Non monetary benefit of holding physical inventory, inferred from the spot futures gap; it spikes on supply scarcity and drives backwardation
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Cost o: Total holding cost of storage, insurance, and financing minus convenience yield linking spot to futures; position versus full carry starts every calendar spread
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Covere: No arbitrage law pinning FX forwards to the rate differential; persistent post 2008 violations create the cross currency basis hedgers pay
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Crop Y: The 12 month marketing window starting at harvest that organizes WASDE balance sheets and defines old crop versus new crop spreads
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Cross: Deviation of FX swap pricing from covered interest parity; persistently negative versus USD, it is the true cost of dollar hedging and a funding stress gauge
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Crude: Density and sulfur content define each crude grade, setting refinery economics and the tradeable quality differentials between light sweet and heavy sour
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Dated: Spot assessment for physical North Sea BFOET cargoes loading 10 to 25 days out; it anchors most global crude formulas, with the CFD spread signaling physical tightness
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Digita: All or nothing option paying a fixed amount if spot finishes past the strike; the simple payoff hides extreme near expiry gamma and unhedgeable pin risk
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/EFS.md: Brent futures minus Dubai swaps, the spread linking Atlantic and Asian crude benchmarks that governs when East to West arbitrage cargoes flow
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Equili: The supply demand balancing level every mean reversion trade targets; a moving anchor whose structural shifts are the biggest risk to reversion bets
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Floati: Storing crude on tankers when contango exceeds charter plus financing; both a contango profit strategy and an AIS trackable leading indicator of oversupply
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Forwar: The strip of futures prices across all delivery dates; the market's pricing of time and the substrate for every commodity relative value trade
Pips added to spot to build the FX forward rate from the interest rate differential; they are the carry a hedger or carry trader pays or receives
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Freigh: Seaborne shipping cost quoted in Worldscale; the gating variable deciding whether cross basin crude arbitrage is economic, and one of the most volatile inputs in commodities
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/GOFO.m: Gold dollar swap rate equal to the dollar rate minus the gold lease rate; rare negative readings signal extreme physical gold scarcity and mark turning points
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Geopol: Oil shocks reprice in a fixed order of vol, skew, flat price, then curve; reading the sequence separates real disruption from headline noise and times the trade
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Gold S: Gold price divided by silver, the classic precious metals relative value metric; readings above 80 favor a long silver short gold reversion over 6 to 18 months
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/ITM.md: An option whose immediate exercise pays, carrying intrinsic value; deep ITM tracks the underlying near delta 100 and decays slowly, a financed substitute for owning it
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Intere: The gap between two countries' benchmark rates, the main driver of FX forward pricing and carry; its expected direction moves spot more than its level
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Intrin: The cash immediate exercise would yield, max(S minus K, 0) for a call; the premium's hard floor that survives to expiry, with the remainder being time value
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Lease: Interest rate for borrowing physical gold, computed as dollar rate minus GOFO; spikes flag physical scarcity and looming short squeezes
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/London: Twice daily LBMA electronic auction setting the benchmark gold price that settles ETFs, derivatives, and reserves; concentrated flow creates tradeable patterns
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Market: Prevailing daily time charter rate you mark open period freight positions against; the freight forward curve compressed into one number
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Moneyn: Relationship between an option's strike and spot spanning ITM, ATM, OTM; sets the intrinsic versus time value split and approximates delta
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/OTM.md: Options with zero intrinsic value and pure time value; cheap convex tail hedges and premium harvesting fodder driven entirely by implied vol
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Old Cr: Price spread between current harvest and next harvest futures; a direct read on present tightness versus expected future balance sheets
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Payoff: Plot of a position's profit against underlying price at expiry; the 4 building block shapes that compose every multi leg strategy
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Physic: Price paid above the exchange benchmark for delivery at a specific location; reveals regional tightness that flat futures cannot show
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Premiu: Upfront price a buyer pays for an option, equal to intrinsic plus time value; the buyer's maximum loss and seller's maximum gain
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Proces: Value of outputs minus cost of inputs earned by whoever runs the conversion asset; the single shape behind crack, crush, and spark spreads
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Purcha: Theory that an identical basket should cost the same across currencies; a slow multi year FX valuation anchor, useless for short term timing
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Put Op: Right to sell the underlying at a fixed strike; capped cost downside insurance for producers, or premium income with large tail risk when sold
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Qualit: Price gap between 2 crude grades differing in API gravity or sulfur; trades refinery economics and regulation with lower vol than flat price
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Real E: Trade weighted, inflation adjusted currency valuation index; mean reverts over 5 to 15 years, making it a value signal but a poor timing tool
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Relati: Position that profits from a change in the price relationship between related instruments rather than outright direction; the core of professional commodity trading
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Reserv: A market maker's inventory adjusted fair value from Avellaneda Stoikov; skews quotes away from mid to attract offsetting flow and shed position
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Risk R: Implied vol difference between a 25 delta call and put; the primary directional skew measure and a near zero cost skew bet
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Roll Y: P&L from rolling a futures position along the curve; backwardation pays carry, contango charges it, often dominating multi month returns
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Scrap: Recycled metal price relative to primary metal; rising primary prices trigger scrap substitution that forms a soft supply ceiling for base metals
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Season: Recurring annual price and spread patterns driven by weather, harvest, and demand cycles; the baseline separating a real signal from noise
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Storag: Costs and capacity of holding physical inventory; caps contango at full carry and drives convenience yield spikes when tanks run empty
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Strike: The fixed transaction price locked at contract creation that anchors an option on the moneyness scale and sets the threshold for exercise, breakeven, and premium outlay
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Sweet: Crude classification by sulfur content where the sweet premium over sour is an actively traded quality spread driven by refinery desulfurization capacity and environmental rules like IMO 2020
Smelter treatment and refining charges that signal concentrate versus smelting capacity balance; collapsing TC/RCs forecast refined copper tightening 3 to 6 months ahead
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Time C: Converts a per tonne voyage into USD per day earnings gross of OPEX so a freight desk can rank a spot voyage against period time charter hire
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Time S: Near minus deferred futures price difference that isolates curve shape from flat price; the most liquid oil spread, positive signals backwardation and near term tightness
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Time V: The premium above intrinsic value that prices the chance of further favorable movement; largest at the money, driven by implied volatility, and decayed to zero at expiry by theta
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Troy O: The 31.1035 gram precious metals unit, 9.7% heavier than the avoirdupois ounce; confusing the two misprices cross exchange gold and silver quotes by nearly 10%
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Uncove: The theory that spot moves offset interest differentials, empirically rejected via the forward premium puzzle; its persistent failure is why carry trades earn 4 to 6% annually
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Vanill: The simplest single strike single expiry call or put; FX quotes it by delta and tenor, and its implied vol defines the surface pricing every exotic
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/War Ri: The per voyage marine insurance charge for transiting a contested chokepoint that becomes a hard per barrel toll, keeping the Brent curve bid even as flat price fades
01-Concepts/pricing-and-valuation/Weathe: The risk buffer built into grain futures during planting and pollination that unwinds 10 to 20% when weather turns favorable; sized inversely to stocks to use
01-Concepts/quantitative/Charm.md: The rate delta drifts as time passes with spot unchanged; leaves a Friday hedged book non neutral by Monday and dominates 0DTE delta management
01-Concepts/quantitative/Color.md: The rate gamma changes as time passes; balloons the hedging cost of any short option in its final week and drives explosive 0DTE gamma growth
01-Concepts/quantitative/Correlation.md: The linear co movement between 2 assets from -1 to +1; foundation of portfolio risk and spread sizing, unstable and spiking toward 1 in crises
01-Concepts/quantitative/Delta.md: Option price change per $1 spot move and approximate ITM probability; the hedge ratio and the axis organizing the FX vol surface
01-Concepts/quantitative/Gamma.md: The rate of change of delta, the payoff curvature; how delta hedged options monetize realized versus implied vol and the core risk of short option books
01-Concepts/quantitative/Greeks.md: The full family of option risk sensitivities from delta to third order; a dashboard mapping how price responds to spot, vol, time, and rates
01-Concepts/quantitative/Kurtosis.md: Tail fatness of a return distribution versus normal; why parametric VaR and Black Scholes understate the frequency of extreme commodity and EM FX moves
The tendency of a price or spread to return to its long run average; foundation of spread trading, valid only for stationary cointegrated series
01-Concepts/quantitative/Momentum Cross: Systematic time series momentum buying recent winners and shorting losers across assets; the core CTA factor, strong in trends and painful at regime turns
01-Concepts/quantitative/Observation Dat: The two date axes of a forward price panel; keying the wrong one turns curve shape into fake returns and silently corrupts every risk number
01-Concepts/quantitative/Realized Volati: The actual annualized standard deviation of past returns; the backward looking benchmark against implied vol that defines the vol risk premium
01-Concepts/quantitative/Rho.md: Option price sensitivity to the risk free rate; a rounding error for short dated options but material for multi year FX and gold options through the forward
01-Concepts/quantitative/Risk Parity.md: Portfolio construction sizing each asset to contribute equal risk; levers low vol bonds and cuts gross exposure across the book when vol spikes
01-Concepts/quantitative/Sharpe Ratio.md: Excess return per unit of return standard deviation; the primary performance metric, scalable by position size, and almost always lower live than in backtest
01-Concepts/quantitative/Skewness.md: The asymmetry of a return distribution; commodities skew positive on supply spikes while FX carry skews negative with violent unwinds
01-Concepts/quantitative/Speed.md: The rate gamma changes as spot moves; explodes near barriers and drives the asymmetric hedging flow behind expiry pinning
01-Concepts/quantitative/Stocks to Use R: Ending inventory divided by annual consumption; the primary tightness gauge for grains, with a convex price relationship that spikes below critical thresholds
01-Concepts/quantitative/Theta.md: The daily decay of an option's time value; the rent a holder pays or a seller collects, accelerating into expiry as the direct tradeoff to gamma
01-Concepts/quantitative/Ultima.md: Third order vol greek, the rate volga changes with vol; negligible in calm markets but dominates deep OTM repricing when vol explodes
01-Concepts/quantitative/Value Cross Ass: Contrarian systematic factor buying below fair value and selling above across FX, commodities, and bonds; slowest factor, naturally hedges momentum crash risk
01-Concepts/quantitative/Vanna.md: Cross greek measuring delta sensitivity to vol; drives FX dealer rehedging flows from exotic books that predictably push spot 20 to 50 pips
01-Concepts/quantitative/Vega.md: Option price sensitivity to a 1 point implied vol move; the dominant risk on any options book and vol's primary tradeable exposure
01-Concepts/quantitative/Veta.md: Rate at which vega bleeds as time passes; thins long vol tail hedges and drives calendar spread P&L even with vol unchanged
01-Concepts/quantitative/Vol Surface.md: 2D map of implied vol across strike and tenor, built in FX from ATM, risk reversal, and butterfly; the pricing engine for every exotic
01-Concepts/quantitative/Vol of Vol.md: Volatility of volatility itself; the tail P&L driver that justifies smile curvature and destroys short vol books when vol regimes flip
01-Concepts/quantitative/Volga.md: Second order greek measuring vega sensitivity to vol; gives OTM wings convexity and sets butterfly pricing, the vanilla way to trade vol of vol
01-Concepts/quantitative/Z-Score.md: Number of standard deviations a reading sits from its mean; the primary mean reversion entry signal that normalizes spreads across units
01-Concepts/quantitative/Zomma.md: Cross greek dGamma/dVol; shifts gamma from ATM toward the wings as vol rises, compounding subsequent spot losses on short OTM positions
01-Concepts/risk/Basis Risk.md: Residual risk left when a hedge instrument differs from the exposure by location, grade, or timing; it converts flat price risk into spread risk
01-Concepts/risk/Bunker Risk.md: Marine fuel price moving against you between fixing a voyage and bunkering; at 40 to 60 percent of voyage cost, it dominates P&L
01-Concepts/risk/Carry Unwind.md: Rapid simultaneous reversal of carry trades on a volatility spike; funding currencies like JPY surge, correlations converge, and months of income vanish in days
01-Concepts/risk/Convexity.md: A nonlinear payoff that gains disproportionately from large moves while losing little on small ones; the shape of risk that decides tail survival
01-Concepts/risk/Correlation Breakdown.m: Sudden shift in cross asset correlations during stress that pushes diversified positions to lose together; the tail risk that undermines risk parity
01-Concepts/risk/Daily Loss Limit.md: Caps how much a desk can lose in one session before trading stops; typically sized at 3 to 5 times daily PnL volatility
01-Concepts/risk/Expected Shortfall.md: Average loss on the days worse than VaR; captures the tail depth VaR ignores and runs 2 to 3 times VaR for fat tailed commodities
01-Concepts/risk/Freight Basis Risk.md: Residual gap left after hedging a physical lane with an index FFA; the wedge between your route and the Baltic basket where hedged freight PnL lands
01-Concepts/risk/Freight Rate Risk.md: Exposure of PnL to changes in the cost of moving cargo by sea; the gating variable that decides whether a location arbitrage clears
01-Concepts/risk/Gap Risk.md: Price jumps discontinuously past where a stop would fill, so realized loss is a multiple of intended risk; only options or being flat protect
01-Concepts/risk/Hard Limit.md: Absolute system enforced threshold that fires the kill switch and may auto flatten on breach; the last line before a firm ending loss
01-Concepts/risk/Hedging.md: Offsetting position that trades large price risk for smaller basis risk plus cost; distinct from relative value by intent, not instrument
01-Concepts/risk/Implied Volatility.md: Market's forward looking price variability backed out of option prices; running 1 to 4 points above realized vol is a persistent premium for sellers
01-Concepts/risk/Inventory Risk.md: Risk that price moves against the inventory a market maker builds while quoting; managed by skewing quotes and fast flattening, not stops
01-Concepts/risk/Kill Switch.md: Emergency mechanism that mass cancels every resting order and blocks new ones in under 100 ms; the panic button that prevents a Knight Capital event
01-Concepts/risk/Leverage.md: Controlling large notional with a sliver of posted capital; a WTI contract runs near 13 times capital, amplifying both PnL and forced liquidation risk
01-Concepts/risk/Liquidity Risk.md: Cannot exit a position at a reasonable price when needed; market and funding illiquidity feed each other and turn hedged spreads into naked bets
01-Concepts/risk/Margin.md: Collateral posted to guarantee futures performance; falling below maintenance triggers a call, and forced deleveraging amplifies moves beyond fundamentals
01-Concepts/risk/Maximum Drawdown.md: Largest peak to trough equity decline before a new high; asymmetric recovery makes it the binding survival constraint, since 50 percent lost needs 100 percent regained
01-Concepts/risk/Overnight Risk.md: Holding through closed or thin hours where you cannot react; combines gap, event, and session liquidity risk, sized at 25 to 50 percent of intraday limits
01-Concepts/risk/Position Limit.md: Maximum contracts held long or short across exchange, regulatory, and internal tiers; prevents cornering and caps single bet loss, smallest limit binds
01-Concepts/risk/Soft Limit.md: Warning threshold at 60 to 80 percent of the hard limit; the yellow light that buys time to cut exposure before a forced kill switch fire sale
01-Concepts/risk/Structural Break.md: Permanent, testable shift in a relationship's parameters; the enemy of mean reversion, since the old mean is gone and reverting to it loses money
01-Concepts/risk/Tail Risk.md: Rare extreme moves far outside what a normal distribution predicts; fat tails make 8 to 10 sigma commodity events routine, favoring convex protection over diversification
01-Concepts/risk/Value at Risk.md: Single number for the loss threshold not breached on X percent of days; a fence around normal losses that says nothing about how far you fall beyond it
01-Concepts/risk/Volatility Smile.md: Pattern of implied vol across strikes at one expiry; its shape reveals which direction the market fears, with commodities often showing positive call skew
01-Concepts/risk/Volatility.md: Standard deviation of returns and the denominator of trading; sets position size, spread valuation, and option prices; clusters and mean reverts
02-Instruments/commodities-agriculture/C: CBOT benchmark (ZC) for feed and ethanol corn; price is set by US Midwest pollination weather, the soybean acreage fight, and WASDE balances
02-Instruments/commodities-agriculture/K: High protein hard red winter bread wheat (KE); the clean Southern Plains drought and protein scarcity trade, best expressed as the spread over Chicago
02-Instruments/commodities-agriculture/S: Raw oilseed at the front of the crush spread; flat price is a proxy for US China trade and the Brazilian harvest, crushed into meal and oil
High protein feed residue from crushing beans (ZM); usually the larger crush product by value, so meal strength pulls the whole soybean complex higher
Vegetable oil crush product (ZL) whose price is set by biofuel mandates and renewable diesel margins more than food; traded against heating oil via BOHO
02-Instruments/commodities-agriculture/W: Chicago soft red winter benchmark (ZW); the most geographically dispersed grain, where Black Sea supply and export politics move price more than US weather
02-Instruments/commodities-energy/Brent: Global seaborne crude benchmark pricing roughly 2/3 of traded oil; a BFOET basket driven by OPEC+ output and Middle East geopolitics, gauged by M1 to M6 backwardation
02-Instruments/commodities-energy/Dubai: Medium sour Middle East to Asia benchmark priced through Platts swaps; the reference for Aramco Asian selling prices, traded against Brent via the EFS spread
02-Instruments/commodities-energy/Henry: US natural gas benchmark (NG) at the Louisiana pipeline hub; the world's cheapest major gas, whose spread to TTF and JKM sets global LNG export flows
02-Instruments/commodities-energy/RBOB G: Unfinished gasoline blendstock (RB) delivered in New York Harbor; the light end of the barrel and most seasonal refined product, driven by summer driving demand and the gasoline crack
02-Instruments/commodities-energy/TTF Na: Main European natural gas benchmark, a virtual Dutch hub priced in euros; driven by Norwegian flows, LNG arrivals, and storage, and arbed against Henry Hub and JKM
02-Instruments/commodities-energy/ULSD H: NYMEX diesel and heating oil contract (HO), the middle of the barrel; the distillate crack reads industrial and freight momentum, with winter heating and export bans as swing factors
02-Instruments/commodities-energy/Urals: Russia's primary medium sour export grade; the Urals Brent discount is the cleanest gauge of sanction enforcement and the 2 tier global oil market
02-Instruments/commodities-energy/WTI Cr: Primary US crude benchmark with physical delivery at landlocked Cushing; storage constraints there drove the negative price of April 2020 and dominate front curve dynamics
02-Instruments/commodities-metals/Alumin: Most traded LME base metal (AH), a proxy for energy and industrial policy since electricity is 30 to 40% of smelting cost and China makes 60% of supply
02-Instruments/commodities-metals/Copper: The most traded base metal, called Dr. Copper because its price leads global growth; China consumes roughly 50% of refined supply
02-Instruments/commodities-metals/Gold F: The only major commodity trading as a monetary asset, pricing real interest rates, USD strength, and safe haven demand simultaneously.
02-Instruments/commodities-metals/Lead F: The least volatile base metal, 85% consumed by lead acid batteries; a 95% recycling rate makes secondary supply dominant and caps upside.
02-Instruments/commodities-metals/Nickel: Volatile metal split between Class 1 battery grade (LME deliverable) and Class 2 stainless steel feed; the 2022 LME squeeze spiked it to $100,000/tonne.
02-Instruments/commodities-metals/Pallad: Catalytic converter metal for gasoline vehicles (85% of demand), Russia and South Africa dominated; EV adoption is flipping it from deficit to surplus.
02-Instruments/commodities-metals/Platin: Precious metal for diesel catalysts, jewelry, and hydrogen fuel cells; South Africa supplies 70%, and it trades at an anomalous discount to gold since 2015.
02-Instruments/commodities-metals/Silver: Dual investment and industrial metal, 50% industrial demand; amplifies gold moves 1.5 to 2x, anchoring the gold silver ratio trade.
02-Instruments/commodities-metals/Tin Fu: The smallest and most illiquid LME base metal, half consumed as electronics solder; thin market plus concentrated supply drives sharp 10 to 20% moves.
02-Instruments/commodities-metals/Zinc F: Galvanizing metal (50% of demand) tied to steel and construction cycles; the lead/zinc ratio is a core relative value pair.
02-Instruments/commodities-softs/Cocoa F: Raw chocolate bean contract; the most volatile soft, with 70% of supply from Ivory Coast and Ghana, so West African weather and disease drive violent supply shocks
02-Instruments/commodities-softs/Coffee: Arabica green coffee (KC); a single Brazilian frost between June and August can move price 20% in a session, and the Arabica Robusta spread is the core softs relative value trade
02-Instruments/commodities-softs/Cotton: ICE No. 2 cotton lint; demand tracks global textiles and GDP rather than food, with polyester substitution above $1/lb capping rallies and Chinese reserve policy dominating
02-Instruments/commodities-softs/Sugar F: ICE No. 11 raw cane sugar; the Brazilian sugar ethanol parity ties it to crude oil, and cane switching is the single most mobile variable in the global supply balance
02-Instruments/equities/S&P 500.md: Float weighted index of 500 large US firms; the cleanest real time read on global risk appetite, inverse to the VIX, driving commodity and FX correlations
02-Instruments/fx/AUD USD.md: The aussie, the most liquid FX proxy for China linked metals demand; tracks iron ore and copper and the RBA versus Fed rate gap
02-Instruments/fx/DXY.md: Geometric weighted USD index against 6 majors, 57.6% euro; the shorthand for broad dollar strength that pressures every USD priced commodity
02-Instruments/fx/EUR USD.md: The most traded pair, near 23% of FX turnover; primary expression of Fed versus ECB divergence and the anchor for the USD complex
02-Instruments/fx/NZD USD.md: The kiwi, cleanest FX proxy for dairy terms of trade through GlobalDairyTrade auctions; a high beta carry currency that shadows AUD/USD
02-Instruments/fx/USD BRL.md: High yielding LatAm pair on Brazil's ag and metals exports and top Selic carry; domestic fiscal shocks, not commodities, usually break the carry
02-Instruments/fx/USD CAD.md: The loonie, quoted inverse; a petrocurrency tracking WTI and the WCS discount plus the BoC versus Fed gap, watch the differential not flat crude
02-Instruments/fx/USD CHF.md: The swissie, haven versus haven; the franc is a gold correlated carry funding currency shaped by an unusually active, intervention prone SNB
02-Instruments/fx/USD CLP.md: The cleanest FX copper proxy, Chile mining a quarter of world copper; tracks the metal and Chinese demand, decouples on mining policy risk
02-Instruments/fx/USD NOK.md: The nokkie, Europe's cleanest liquid oil currency on Brent; thin and high beta, gaps hard in risk off with recurring GPFG sovereign fund flows
02-Instruments/fx/USD ZAR.md: Rand per dollar, a high beta emerging market carry pair that trades as a gold and platinum export proxy and sells off first in any risk off move
02-Instruments/rates/US 10Y Treasury.md: 10 year US government note whose yield anchors global discount rates, the dollar, and gold; high duration, traded through CBOT ZN futures
02-Instruments/rates/US 2Y Treasury.md: Front end US note, the most Fed policy sensitive point on the curve; cleanest read on the expected rate path, low duration, traded via ZT
03-Markets/CLS.md: FX settlement system that eliminates Herstatt risk by settling both currency legs simultaneously; clears over $6 trillion daily across 18 currencies.
03-Markets/COMEX.md: CME's primary metals futures exchange where US hours price discovery happens; its COT positioning data is the key gold and silver sentiment gauge.
03-Markets/EEXI and CII Regulations.md: IMO carbon rules forcing slow steaming: EEXI caps engine power once, CII grades annual efficiency; both remove effective tonnage and tighten freight supply.
03-Markets/LBMA.md: London OTC market for wholesale physical gold and silver; sets the twice daily benchmark price and the Good Delivery bar standard the world references.
03-Markets/LME.md: Premier base metals exchange with a unique daily prompt date system; its cash to 3 month spread is the key physical tightness indicator.
03-Markets/SHFE.md: China's yuan denominated metals futures exchange; the SHFE to LME price gap, adjusted for VAT and freight, drives physical import flows.
03-Markets/Strait of Hormuz.md: The most important energy chokepoint, carrying roughly 20% of global oil; disruption threats add $5 to $15/barrel of crude risk premium.
04-Strategies/00 Strategies index.md: Map of content hub linking every strategy playbook in the vault, grouped by type, separating executable trades from their underlying concepts.
04-Strategies/relative-value/Arabica-Rob: Trades the quality gap between Arabica (KC) and Robusta (RC) coffee; roaster substitution anchors mean reversion, but Brazil frost can blow it open.
04-Strategies/relative-value/Brent-WTI S: Prices the gap between seaborne Brent and landlocked WTI at Cushing; anchored by transportation economics, it mean reverts unless infrastructure regimes shift.
04-Strategies/relative-value/Calendar Sp: Buys one delivery month and sells another of the same commodity, isolating forward curve shape while cancelling most directional price risk.
04-Strategies/relative-value/Cash and Ca: Buy spot, store it, and sell a future to lock a fixed carry profit; this arb caps contango, with storage the binding constraint.
04-Strategies/relative-value/Cocoa NY-Lo: Trades ICE US cocoa minus London cocoa converted to dollars, capturing bean quality differentials, GBP/USD moves, and regional grind demand
04-Strategies/relative-value/Crack Sprea: Refiner's gross margin, refined product value minus crude cost; both a margin hedge and a real time read on crude demand
04-Strategies/relative-value/Crush Sprea: Soybean processing margin, meal plus oil value minus bean cost; the agricultural twin of the crack spread, quoted in cents per bushel
04-Strategies/relative-value/Gasoline Cr: RBOB minus crude refining margin, the most seasonal energy spread; widens into US summer driving season from spring lows
04-Strategies/relative-value/Gold-Copper: Gold divided by copper as a single fear versus growth gauge; rising ratio signals fear, falling signals industrial optimism
04-Strategies/relative-value/Heating Cra: Middle distillate minus crude refining margin, ULSD or gasoil; widens on Northern Hemisphere winter heating and tracks industrial diesel demand
04-Strategies/relative-value/Henry Hub-T: US versus European gas price gap, anchored by the full chain LNG netback cost that decides whether cargoes sail to Europe
04-Strategies/relative-value/Inter-Commo: Long one commodity, short a related one; profits from relative pricing anchored by processing, substitution, or shared demand linkage
04-Strategies/relative-value/KC-Chicago: Hard red winter minus soft red winter wheat, the market price of milling protein and Southern Plains drought; reverts only at harvest
04-Strategies/relative-value/Location Ar: Same commodity priced at different locations; the spread is bounded by transport cost and closes when physical flows respond
04-Strategies/relative-value/Platinum-Pa: Two metals doing the same catalytic converter job; substitution at price extremes gives the spread a structural ceiling and floor
04-Strategies/relative-value/Relet.md: Charter a ship in at fixed hire, employ it out on voyages, and pocket the TCE minus hire margin; structurally long freight
04-Strategies/relative-value/SHFE vs LME: Chinese versus international base metal prices after VAT, freight, and FX; the import parity window driving physical metal flows into China
04-Strategies/relative-value/Scrubber Sp: VLSFO minus HSFO marine fuel spread (Hi5), the per tonne saving that decides whether a scrubber retrofit pays or strands capex
04-Strategies/relative-value/Soybean-Cor: Soybean divided by corn, the acreage battle ratio that mean reverts through spring planting decisions hitting supply 6 months later
04-Strategies/relative-value/Spread Trad: Simultaneous long and short in 2 related contracts, profiting from the price difference not direction; lower volatility, margin, and risk
04-Strategies/relative-value/Sugar-Ethan: Brazilian mill mix, sugar parity versus ethanol parity per tonne of cane, carrying a hidden oil beta through the pump
04-Strategies/volatility/Straddle.md: Long ATM call plus put at one strike, the purest volatility bet; the benchmark FX option quote at each tenor
04-Strategies/volatility/Strangle.md: Long OTM call plus put at 25 delta strikes, cheaper than a straddle but needs a bigger move; the butterfly building block
04-Strategies/volatility/Variance Swap.m: Pure realized variance bet with no direction, delta, or theta; squaring returns means one shock dominates and destroys the short
05-People-and-Firms/CTA.md: Systematic managed futures manager, mostly trend following across all liquid futures; largest systematic commodity participant, prized for crisis alpha
05-People-and-Firms/OPEC+.md: Broader oil coalition of the 13 OPEC members plus 10 partners including Russia, controlling roughly 50% of global output; its internal fractures cause the largest supply shocks.
05-People-and-Firms/OPEC.md: Cartel of 13 producers setting quotas over roughly 30% of global crude, with Saudi Arabia as swing producer; Vienna meetings move Brent $3 to $10 in a session.
05-People-and-Firms/Trafigura.md: One of the largest independent physical trading houses, asset backed and employee owned; its edge is logistics, financing, and arbitrage, hedging every barrel on paper to isolate basis.
06-Data-and-Indicators/API Report.md: Unofficial Tuesday 4:30 PM ET petroleum inventory print from the industry trade group that previews the EIA by 18 hours and moves overnight WTI.
06-Data-and-Indicators/Baltic Exchange a: London panel assessed dry bulk freight benchmarks whose BDI blends Capesize, Panamax, and Supramax sub indices and sets the settlement reference for Forward Freight Agreements.
06-Data-and-Indicators/Baltic Route Code: Standardised labels like C3 and P2A that fix cargo, vessel size, and port pair for one voyage, defining exactly what an FFA settles against and where basis risk hides.
06-Data-and-Indicators/COT Positioning.m: Percentile analysis of managed money net length from the CFTC report; extremes above the 90th or below the 10th mark crowded trades vulnerable to a catalyst driven unwind.
06-Data-and-Indicators/COT Report.md: Weekly CFTC breakdown of US futures open interest by trader category, released Friday for Tuesday positions; the standard source for spotting crowded speculative extremes.
06-Data-and-Indicators/China PMI.md: Monthly manufacturing survey (NBS and Caixin) of the largest base metals consumer where the surprise versus consensus, not the level, moves copper, AUD, and iron ore.
06-Data-and-Indicators/Dollar Index.md: Weighted geometric mean of USD against 6 currencies, 58% EUR, unchanged since 1973; the daily read on broad dollar strength with inverse correlation to commodities.
06-Data-and-Indicators/EIA Report.md: Official Wednesday 10:30 AM ET US petroleum status report, the highest frequency energy release; the deviation from consensus, with Cushing stocks separate, moves WTI within seconds.
06-Data-and-Indicators/ETF Flows.md: Daily change in physical metal held by precious metal ETFs like GLD; the visible investment demand gauge that separates real money rallies from fragile speculative ones.
06-Data-and-Indicators/FX Fix.md: The WM/Reuters 4PM London benchmark, a 5 minute median that anchors index rebalancing flows; the most important recurring microstructure event in global FX.
06-Data-and-Indicators/ICCO.md: Intergovernmental cocoa body publishing quarterly grindings and annual surplus or deficit forecasts; its deficit revisions steepen the curve into backwardation, cocoa's answer to WASDE.
Certified cocoa in ICE warehouses deliverable against futures, the tightest measure of immediately available supply; falling stocks near expiry drive front month backwardation.
06-Data-and-Indicators/IEA.md: Paris consumer side agency whose monthly Oil Market Report drives medium term positioning; demand and supply revisions move 6 to 24 month calendar spreads, not the front.
06-Data-and-Indicators/LME Warehouse Sto: Daily visible base metals inventory in LME approved warehouses; rate of change and the cancelled warrant ratio flag physical demand and looming squeezes before metal moves.
06-Data-and-Indicators/VIX.md: CBOE index of expected 30 day SPX volatility from a model free option strip; the fear gauge and risk on risk off thermometer that triggers cross asset carry unwinds above 25.
06-Data-and-Indicators/VVIX.md: Implied volatility of VIX options, the vol of vol; a high VVIX with calm VIX signals quiet tail hedging that often precedes a volatility spike and carry unwind.
06-Data-and-Indicators/WASDE.md: USDA monthly global crop balance sheet released near the 10th; the ending stocks and stocks to use figures routinely swing corn, wheat, and soybeans 3 to 5% within minutes.
06-Data-and-Indicators/West African Port: Weekly cocoa bean arrivals at Ivory Coast and Ghana ports, the highest frequency supply indicator; cumulative shortfalls versus prior seasons front run ICCO production estimates.
07-Infrastructure/API.md: Structured message interface connecting trading systems to exchanges, brokers, and data providers, where FIX and WebSocket carry order flow while slow REST handles reference data
07-Infrastructure/Branch Prediction.md: CPU guesses which side of a conditional runs; each misprediction costs 5 to 7 ns, and data dependent pricing branches defeat it unless rewritten branchless
07-Infrastructure/Cache Locality.md: Laying out data contiguously so the CPU reads from 1 ns cache rather than 100 ns RAM; arrays over linked structures keeps the hot path fast
07-Infrastructure/Cache Miss.md: CPU stall when requested data is absent from cache; an L3 miss to RAM costs roughly 100 ns and can double tick to trade
07-Infrastructure/Co-location.md: Placing servers inside the exchange data center to cut round trip latency to microseconds versus tens of milliseconds remote; table stakes for electronic market making
07-Infrastructure/Cold Path.md: The periodic non latency critical part of a system handling risk, P&L, and reporting in Python, feeding recalibrated parameters to the hot path
07-Infrastructure/Data Feed.md: Live exchange stream of prices, sizes, and trades; Level 1 shows top of book while Level 2 shows full depth, and stale feeds trade on phantom prices
07-Infrastructure/FIX Protocol.md: Standardized tag=value messaging format for orders, cancels, fills, and market data; the lingua franca connecting firms to every major exchange and ECN
07-Infrastructure/Garbage Collection.md: Automatic memory reclamation in Java and Python that triggers stop the world pauses of milliseconds; why the hot path uses C++ or Rust instead
07-Infrastructure/Heartbeat.md: Periodic keep alive message confirming a connection is live; its real job is detecting silent disconnects while resting orders remain exposed on the exchange
07-Infrastructure/Hot Path.md: The code executing on every tick where nanoseconds decide queue position; ruthlessly optimized with no allocation, logging, or system calls
07-Infrastructure/Jitter.md: Variance in latency measured as P99 minus P50; the freeze spikes are exactly when fast competitors snipe your stale quotes
07-Infrastructure/Latency Units.md: The millisecond, microsecond, and nanosecond scales for measuring system speed; knowing which applies to each stage prevents mismatched architecture and budgets
07-Infrastructure/Latency.md: Round trip delay between sending a message and receiving acknowledgement; physics floors wire latency at 5 microseconds per kilometer, so only colocation truly fixes it
07-Infrastructure/Memory Allocation.md: Reserving RAM at runtime; malloc costs 100 to 500 ns with unpredictable tail spikes, so hot paths pre allocate object pools at startup
07-Infrastructure/Throughput.md: Messages per second a system can process, distinct from per message latency; insufficient capacity queues messages during volatility spikes and produces stale quotes
07-Infrastructure/Tick to Trade.md: Total time from a market data update hitting the NIC to the resulting order leaving it; the single metric that sets passive queue position
07-Infrastructure/execution/Execution Al: Slice large parent orders into timed child orders to minimize market impact and slippage across benchmark, aggressive, and passive families
07-Infrastructure/execution/Implementati: Perold's gap between the decision price and realized execution, capturing market impact, timing drift, spread, fees, and opportunity cost from unfilled quantity
07-Infrastructure/execution/POV.md: Execution algo that trades a fixed fraction of real time market volume, speeding up when active and slowing when quiet without needing a volume forecast
07-Infrastructure/execution/Smart Order: Automatically splits each order across fragmented venues by price, depth, fees, latency, and fill probability; decides where while execution algos decide when
07-Infrastructure/execution/TCA.md: Post trade measurement of execution quality against VWAP, arrival, or close benchmarks; decomposes cost into spread, impact, timing, and opportunity to grade algos, brokers, and venues
07-Infrastructure/execution/TWAP.md: Execution algorithm that slices an order into equal pieces at fixed time intervals ignoring volume; preferred for lumpy commodity liquidity and 24 hour FX where it resists gaming
07-Infrastructure/execution/VWAP.md: Volume weighted average price serving as both the standard institutional execution benchmark and an algorithm that paces child orders proportional to expected volume per bucket
